items.title: Sharks’ Celebrini fifth-youngest player in NHL history to reach 200 career points
items.summary: Sidney Crosby, Wayne Gretzky, Jimmy Carson and Mario Lemieux are the only players to hit the milestone at a younger age.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images Macklin Celebrini has found himself in rare air. During the San Jose Sharks ‘ 3-2 shootout loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday , Celebrini hit the 200-point milestone in his career, becoming the fifth-youngest player to reach that threshold. Celebrini achieved the feat midway through the third period of the game, when an offensive zone sequence saw Will Smith pass the puck across the zone to Michael Kesselring, who had previously pinched up on the breakout rush and was still deep in the zone. Kesselring immediately bumped the puck towards Celebrini in the high slot, who faked the first shot to trick the defense and goalie before firing home a goal to cut Pittsburgh’s 2-1 lead in half and giving him his 200th career point. Celebrini then followed it up with the primary assist on Mason Marchment’s game-tying goal with a bit over four minutes to go in the third period, giving him his 201st point. With his 200th point, Celebrini became the fifth-youngest player to reach the milestone, doing so at the age of 20 years and 151 days. He joins some elite players in the process, with the four players ahead of him being Mario Lemieux (20 years, 133 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days), Wayne Gretzky (19 years, 347 days) and Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days). Admittedly, Celebrini and Crosby do have an advantage to get there in a similar amount of time to the likes of Gretzky and Lemieux, as the two have birthdays closer to the cut-off date for draft eligibility, with Celebrini’s being June 13th and Crosby’s being August 7th. items.title: Oilers beat Flyers in OT as goaltending shows signs of stability
items.summary: After consecutive wins where an Oilers goalie was the best player on the ice, it’s starting to look like Edmonton might finally have found some stability in the crease.
items.body: EDMONTON — Back in 1987, when the Edmonton Oilers would win a Stanley Cup off a season in which their team save percentage was .881, Grant Fuhr taught us that there was only one stat that truly mattered. And it starts with a ‘W’. But the game changed along the way, and as the Oilers careened from Mikko Koskinen to Connor Ingram, from Mike Smith to Stuart Skinner, we realized that perhaps it was an environment issue in Edmonton as much as it was about the quality of the netminders. Well, after consecutive games where an Oilers goalie was the best player on the ice, Edmonton might finally have something here. Tristan Jarry stopped 30 shots, Evan Bouchard scored the OT winner, and for the second straight game the visitors were the better team yet lost, as the Oilers beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2. “Good teams ... what they do is find ways to win,” said head coach Mike Babcock. “They rely on their structure even when it's a disaster. You're five tight (around the net) and doing good things. “Jars made tons of good saves, but he didn't have to go east-west a ton. There weren't lateral feeds ... the (shot attempts) were coming right at him. As bad as we were we still did OK that way.” When the 27th-place team comes into your building and spanks you as badly as the Flyers did the Oilers — as of this morning, the No. 1 team in the NHL with 31 points in 20 games — it can’t all be good, however. items.body: Forward says he’s happy playing for Philadelphia, can be restricted free agent after season Daniel Briere said the report of Matvei Michkov wanting to play elsewhere “was not correct,” and the Philadelphia Flyers general manager expects the forward to be a big part of their team now and in the future. “Part of the reason why we’re in Edmonton is this morning we got a chance to meet up with Matvei and Matvei said (the report) wasn’t from him. He never said anything about that. He doesn’t know where it came from, who it was from,” Briere said Wednesday. “We also spoke to his agent, and his agent swears it wasn’t from him either. “Matvei attracts a lot of attention and rightfully so. He’s been having a good season. He showed up this year, he’s done everything we’ve asked of him, and he started the season really well. People want to know more about him. So, when there’s a report like this today (about) a player we expect to be here for a long, long time and part of the solution for the long term, it’s important to step in front of it and adjust what’s been out there.” Michkov said earlier in the day that he’s happy playing for the Flyers and not paying attention to news reports that he wants to play somewhere else. "I don't read all the news. I don't want to talk or interview," Michkov said in Edmonton. "I need concentration on just tonight's game and that's all." items.summary: The only thing missing from Zayne Parekh’s goal-of-the-year candidate was, um, the goal. Otherwise, he would have been a frontrunner.
items.body: CALGARY — The only thing missing from Zayne Parekh ’s goal-of-the-year candidacy was, um, the goal. On a night in which the 20-year-old Flames defenceman stole most of the game’s thunder with a couple sassy forays, it was an audacious play by Parekh early on that had everyone shaking their heads in amazement the rest of the night. It’s guaranteed to be Thursday’s water cooler talk around town, too. The Flames finally appear to have a player that fans can identify as the one they’d pay the price of admission for. And, boy, on Wednesday night did they get their money’s worth. items.title: Ducks’ Gauthier matches 105-year-old record with goal vs. Predators
items.body: The Anaheim Ducks forward continued his November scoring spree with a goal against the Nashville Predators on Wednesday night — his 14th tally in his last seven games. He became the first NHL player to achieve that feat since Mario Lemieux and Alexander Mogilny did so in the 1992-93 season. Gauthier also tied a 105-year-old record with the goal, becoming the first player since Punch Broadbent and Joe Malone in 1921-22 to score 12 games in his team's first six games of a calendar month. The 22-year-old already has three hat tricks this month, potting a trio of goals against the Ottawa Senators on Nov. 1, the Vancouver Canucks on Nov. 3 and the Pittsburgh Penguins on Sunday. In 2025-26, Gauthier had 41 goals and 28 assists in 76 games for the Ducks.

items.body: Mika Zibanejad scored twice in the second period on Wednesday to lead the New York Rangers to a 3-1 victory over the Calgary Flames . Tye Kartye, into an empty net, also scored for New York (11-8-1). The Rangers have won four of their last five. items.title: Kucherov has natural hat trick in Lightning romp over Sabres
items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Nikita Kucherov had a natural hat trick and an assist — all in the third period — and the Tampa Bay Lightning beat the Buffalo Sabres 8-3 on Wednesday night for their fourth victory in five games. Kucherov, the Russian star who requested a trade Oct. 30, had his eighth NHL hat trick after the Sabres scored three in a row to cut it to 4-3. Brandon Hagel scored twice, John Carlson had a goal and four assists, and Scott Sabourin and Yanni Gourde also scored. Jake Guentzel had four assists, and Anthony Cirelli added three, and Andrei Vasilevskiy made 28 saves. Josh Doan, Jason Zucker and Tage Thompson scored for the Sabres, who have lost three of their last four. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made nine saves on 14 shots and Colten Ellis stopped five of eight shots in relief. Thompson cut it to 4-3 33 seconds into the third period, but Kucherov soon took over, scoring his first two in a 2:46 span.

This move comes after Safonov left the AHL’s Abbotsford Canucks to rejoin the KHL’s Ak Bars Kazan. Safonov released a statement through his agent, Dan Milstein, citing his failure to crack the NHL roster as a driver of his decision. Vancouver signed Safonov to a one-year, $950K contract over the summer. That deal moved the 6-foot-4 forward away from six years in Kazan’s pipeline. He joined Kazan’s junior team ahead of the 2018-19 season and earned a call-up to the VHL – Russia’s second-tier pro league – in the same year. The KHL came one season later, beginning Safonov’s slow climb to a productive pro role. He scored four points in 37 games of his rookie KHL season in 2020-21. While a quiet start to his career, his established pro role pushed the Chicago Blackhawks to draft Safonov in the sixth-round of the 2021 NHL Draft – his third and final year of draft eligibility. Safonov was named Ak Bars’ alternate captain, and scored a career-high 37 points in 64 games, two seasons later. That peak was followed by a pair of quiet seasons – though 22 points in 51 games of the 2024-25 campaign pushed Vancouver to acquire Safonov’s rights in exchange for future considerations ahead of the 2025 NHL Draft. He scored 33 points in 68 games in the following season, leading up to his first NHL contract. Safonov will now leave the Canucks’ organization after five months. Winger Anthony Mantha has been moved from injured reserve to long-term injured reserve as he continues to recover from a throat injury. That scoring brought his year-long totals up to 10 points, split evenly, in 17 games. Mantha managed that production despite averaging 13:28 in ice time, offering New Jersey invaluable scoring down the lineup. The Devils broke up their third-line – consisting of Mantha, Evan Rodrigues , and Jesper Boqvist – following Mantha’s injury. items.body: CHICAGO — Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson defended coach Jeff Blashill on Wednesday while taking responsibility for the team's lacklustre start. Davidson also said Mark Eaton is going to be embedded with the coaching staff for the foreseeable future to help improve individual defensive skills for one of the NHL's worst defensive teams. Eaton, a former NHL defenseman, is the team's assistant general manager for player development. Heading into this season, Davidson and several Chicago players talked about contending for a playoff spot. But the Blackhawks are off to a 4-13-1 start after dropping six in a row and nine of 10 overall. “Simply put, we’ve not been good enough,” Davidson said. “This isn’t what we told our fans to expect. And, you know, I take responsibility in this and I’m not going to come up here today and make any excuses.” Chicago concluded an ugly three-game trip with a 9-2 loss at Carolina on Saturday night. The Blackhawks had four days off after the matchup with the Hurricanes, leading to speculation about Blashill's future in his second season with the franchise, but Davidson decided to keep the team's coaching staff in place. “Blash is our head coach,” Davidson said. “I have full confidence in him. items.summary: Wotherspoon has missed 13 games after suffering an upper-body injury on October 10.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vegas Golden Knights are getting a little healthier on the blueline. On Wednesday, the Golden Knights activated defenseman Parker Wotherspoon off of injured reserve, with the expectation that he will suit up for Vegas’ home game against the Utah Mammoth . The Surrey, British Columbia native’s return is a welcome sight for the Golden Knights, as they remain without defensemen Alex Pietrangelo and Noah Hanifin due to injury. Wotherspoon, 29, has missed Vegas’ last 13 games after suffering an upper-body injury during a 2-1 overtime win against the Los Angeles Kings on October 10. In six games played this season, Wotherspoon has gone scoreless while averaging just over 18 minutes of ice time. The Golden Knights acquired Wotherspoon this past offseason from the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for defenseman Kaedan Korczak, with Pittsburgh retaining half of his $1 million cap hit for this season. Last season with the Penguins, Wotherspoon notched three goals and 27 assists for a career-best 30 points in 80 games, before contributing no goals and an assist during Pittsburgh’s first-round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Flyers in six games. In the long and storied history of the Hart Memorial Trophy, which is awarded annually to the NHL's most-valuable regular-season player, a pattern has emerged. And if you're a defenseman in hockey’s top league, that pattern isn't a good one. It's been more than a quarter century since a D-man has been honored with the award. "There's always the barometer of who you're up against. And in some cases, you're going up against someone on your team. If you're able to do that, then someone on your team is having a career year as well." items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Vancouver Canucks announced Wednesday that forward Ilya Safonov was placed on unconditional waivers for the purpose of contract termination. He was traded to the Canucks after the 2024-25 season, then signed a one-year, two-way contract with Vancouver last summer. But 12 games into the North American portion of his professional career, he has just four assists with Abbotsford. Safonov, a native of Moscow, had 16 goals and 17 assists for 33 points in 68 games with Kazan Ak-Bars in the KHL. He also had two goals and seven assists for nine points in 20 Gagarin Cup games. His best season came in 2022-23, he posted a career-high 19 goals and 18 assists for 37 points and was named a KHL All-Star. Their 4-13-1 start has them in 31st place in the NHL standings, and they are one of just two teams that has yet to reach 10 points in the standings. Things bottomed out on Saturday with a 9-2 loss on the road against the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . With four days off between games, Davidson held a media availability to share an update on his pursuit of moves to improve the team and better position it to bounce back as the season moves along. “I’ve made it clear around the league that we’re intent on improving the playing roster,” Davidson told reporters, including Ben Pope of The Chicago Sun Times . “This is a precarious time where you don’t want to do something to do something and make a mistake you’ll regret later.” Davidson was active this summer in adding experienced pieces in a bid to improve a roster that has plenty of young talent but has failed to advance past the non-competitive stage of a rebuild. The multi-week upper-body injury has limited him to six games with his new club. He’s gone scoreless in those six contests, with a -6 rating and a dismal 82.1% on-ice SV%. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A notable update after a massive collision on Tuesday night. When speaking to the media on Wednesday, Ottawa Senators head coach Travis Green revealed that forward Nick Cousins will miss at least a week to 10 days after taking a huge hit from Washington Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun. The play that put Cousins on the shelf came late in the third period at Canadian Tire Center. Cousins was looking to break the puck out of the Ottawa zone, but was leveled by Chychrun, who was pinching in from the left point. The hit sent Cousins soaring into the glass before falling flat to the ice. Cousins was left motionless on the ice before receiving assistance from the Senators’ training staff. He was taken off the ice and immediately brought to the team’s dressing room. He didn’t return to the game. No penalty was called on the play. Green confirmed what many who saw the hit believed, and that was the fact that Cousins was knocked out on the ice after the check. Tuesday night’s contest was Cousin’s 19th appearance of the 2026-27 season. The veteran center has struggled to find his offensive touch, scoring just two goals and three points thus far. He has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:45 of ice time, amassing 44 penalty minutes. The Senators wrap up their quick home swing on Thursday night, hosting the Colorado Avalanche. This comes not long after Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stated that Russia “will not” be at the World Juniors, which are set to begin on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer. The whole debate on whether Russia would be allowed to play in the upcoming event came after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation must be allowed to compete in IIHF events, citing that the IIHF didn’t provide enough evidence to keep the ban on Russian teams in place. The IIHF, along with numerous international hockey federations, has voiced its displeasure on the decision. Nations have come forward, stating that they won’t play Russia in any international events, with some big-time sponsors threatening to pull their funding from the IIHF, if Russia is allowed to compete. As it stands, Norway, the last-ranked team heading into the WJC, has been informed that it will be removed from the tournament to make way for Russia . However, many expect Russia to be forced to back out, leading to Norway’s readmission to the event. The ban on Russian hockey teams dates back to 2022, when the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the Beijing Olympics.

items.title: Senators’ Cousins out at least one week after hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: Nick Cousins won't be back on the ice for the next little while. The Ottawa Senators enforcer is out at least one week after absorbing a massive hit from Washington Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun on Tuesday, head coach Travis Green told reporters Wednesday. Cousins was briefly knocked out by the play, Green said. No penalty was called. Washington went on to win 3-2 in overtime. As Cousins looked to clear the puck out of the defensive end late in the third period, Chychrun caught him with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face-down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He did not return. "He's not doing great," Green said after the game, adding that Cousins did not go to the hospital. "I thought it was a head shot to a player who wasn't ready for it. They must have saw it different." The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined there was no penalty. "I should be careful what I say; I don't like seeing that stuff," Senators forward Ridly Greig said. Added captain Thomas Chabot: "I hate, I think everybody hates, these scenes in hockey, in any sport." Cousins, 33, has two goals and one assist in 19 games this season. The Senators are back in action Thursday at home against the Colorado Avalanche.

items.body: Saw Carolina play as a 13-year-old, now facing Kraken in Global Series HELSINKI -- Sebastian Aho is living a dream that took shape 16 years ago. He was 13 years old and found himself at Hartwall Arena -- the mecca of Finnish hockey and home to the Finnish national ice hockey team -- to watch the Carolina Hurricanes take on the Minnesota Wild in the 2010 NHL Premiere Series. The trip from his home in Oulu to the Finnish capital is about seven hours by car, but for Aho it may as well have been a different world. items.summary: The message from Daniel Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Matvei Michkov.
items.body: TORONTO — Despite a report about Matvei Michkov’s apparent unhappiness and potential interest in a change of scenery, the Philadelphia Flyers say they have not received a request for a trade from Michkov’s agent and were surprised by the news. “This is all news to me,” Flyers general manager Daniel Briere said. Beyond that, the message from Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Michkov. “No, that’s not the plan at all,” Briere said. “We’ve never discussed that.” The report from NHL Network ’s Kevin Weekes cited “internal turmoil” with the Flyers as part of Michkov’s interest in “wanting a new start elsewhere,” but earlier on Wednesday following the GM Meetings in downtown Toronto, Briere took zero issue with Michkov’s emotion that spilled over to the bench during an in-game confrontation with teammate Nick Seeler. “I actually like the fact that our guys are fiery and they want to win,” Briere said. “That’s what I saw [in Vancouver]. It’s showing competitive players. That’s what we’re looking for, that’s what we want. The reality is, the team hasn’t performed great this year and players expect more out of themselves.” Briere scoffed at the notion that the in-game quarrelling over a sequence in the offensive zone had any indication that the Flyers were lacking in the culture department, as some observers have suggested. “If we had a culture where guys are yelling at each other and no one is responding, a culture that guys don’t care about winning, then we’d be in trouble,” Briere said. “But when you show a culture that guys want to better themselves and they’re not happy where they are, I expect that.” One of the most emotional and competitive players on the last great Flyers teams, Briere said he was glad there weren’t as many cameras as there are now.

As gruesome as the hit was, all the video angles suggest that it was a shoulder-on-chest hit, which is perfectly legal physicality. Chychrun was not assessed a penalty for the hit. Unsurprisingly, Senators head coach Travis Green didn’t have a positive prognosis for Cousins after the game, although further evaluation hadn’t been finished. According to Julian McKenzie of The Athletic , Green said, “ He’s not doing great. ” Before leaving last night’s game, Cousins had scored two goals and three points in 19 games for Ottawa this season, and had delivered 42 hits of his own while accruing 44 PIMs. Meanwhile, Chychrun is unlikely to receive any additional disciplinary action. He’s not known for his physicality, and he has maintained a clean record with the NHL’s Department of Player Safety throughout his 11-year career. Still, despite being less physical than most, he’s certainly not someone you’d want to catch you with your head down, as he stands at 6’3″, 215lbs. items.title: Report: Wild’s Brock Faber expected to make season debut Saturday
items.summary: Faber suffered a fractured skull and underwent surgery during the preseason and has been out of the lineup since September
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber is on track to make his regular-season debut Saturday night against the Boston Bruins , according to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli . Faber, 24, has been out of the lineup late September after he suffered a fractured skull in a preseason game and underwent surgery . The Wild placed Faber on injured reserve and said there was no timetable yet on a return. Faber is coming off a 2025-26 campaign that saw him record 15 goals and 36 assists for 51 points in 80 games, averaging 24:41 of ice time per game. He also had four goals and six assists for 10 pogints in 11 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. In three full NHL seasons, Faber, a 2020 second-round pick, has 33 goals and 94 assists for 127 points in 242 career regular-season games, averaging 25:01 of ice time during that span. A native of Maple Grove, Minn., Faber also helped the U.S. men’s hockey team earn a gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Italy. He also earned a gold medal at the 2021 World Junior Championships. Faber played three seasons of college hockey at the University of Minnesota. In 97 career NCAA games, he scored seven goals and added 46 assists for 53 points. The Wild are 13-3-4 with 30 points in their first 20 games of 2026-27, which going into Wednesday’s slate of action ranks first among all NHL teams . Forward Kirill Kaprizov is second in the league in goals with 17 and third in points with 32. Meanwhile, defenseman Quinn Hughes is tied for third among all skaters with 21 assists and tied for seventh in points with 27.

items.title: Finland’s Jenni Hiirikoski becomes first to play 100 games at IIHF Women’s Worlds
items.summary: Hiirikoski has been a mainstay at the WWC since debuting with Finland back in 2004.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: (Photo by Steven Ellis/Daily Faceoff) One of the most talented and well-respected players in women’s hockey has made history. When the puck dropped on the final day of the group stage of the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship in Herning, Denmark on Wednesday, Finland defender Jenni Hiirikoski became the first player to appear in 100 games in the tournament’s history. Hiirikoski also became just the 12th player, male or female, to play in 100 games in a world championship career. The next closest player behind her in games played at the WWC is United States Captain Hilary Knight, who will be making her 91st appearance when the Americans play Czechia later on Wednesday. The Lempäälä native has been a mainstay on the Finnish national team since she debuted at the Women’s Worlds all the way back in 2004. Since then, she has become not only one of the best players to come out of Finland, but is also widely regarded as one of the top blueliners ever to lace up her skates. She has helped Finland reach incredible heights over the last two decades, and has been a leader for Finnish hockey ever since she was named team captain prior to the 2012 World Championship. In her first 99 appearances across 17 tournaments, Hiirikoski has scored 15 goals, 45 assists for 60 points. She’s the all-time leading scorer by a defender at the WWC, and is tied for second all time in scoring by a Finn at the World Championships with Hockey Hall of Famer Riikka Sallinen. She’s just three points back of her teammate Michelle Karvinen. items.body: Register Login The Kings Botched Their Once Promising Rebuild By Josh Cybulski | at November 11, 2026 8:00 am The Los Angeles Kings spent the last 2010s and early 2020s pivoting from the most successful era in franchise history to what was supposed to be their next great era of hockey, and for a while, it looked like success was just a matter of time. The Kings assembled the best prospect system in the entire NHL by 2021 ( according to Scott Wheeler of The Athletic ), led by Quinton Byfield , Alex Turcotte, and Arthur Kaliyev , but have since squandered their potential and are now one of the worst teams in the NHL. Even worse, their roster is an aging, expensive disaster. It’s almost inexplicable that, just five years later, the Kings have the oldest team in the NHL, with an average age of 31. No single issue caused this downfall; it was a series of bad trades, poor development, and aggressive management decisions. The amazing thing for Los Angeles is that they were primed to build a sustainable contender around Byfield and Brandt Clarke , but now find themselves in a position where the playoffs feel like a long shot and their contention window is nearly closed. There was obviously an opportunity for the Kings to be great, but for whatever reason, management’s mandate shifted to aggressively pursuing veterans and trading away much of their future to do so. In a vacuum, many of the Kings’ moves were fine, but when you sacrifice the future for the present, you need deals to work out better than just okay. A good example is the Kevin Fiala deal with the Minnesota Wild. items.summary: NEW YORK – The National Hockey League (NHL), Buffalo Sabres, and Vegas Golden Knights today announced they have erased $1.5 million of debt for U.S. veterans in recognition of Veterans Day. The NHL’s partnership with ForgiveCo will provide debt relief and aid to more than 600 veterans and their families.
items.body: NEW YORK – The National Hockey League (NHL), Buffalo Sabres, and Vegas Golden Knights today announced they have erased $1.5 million of debt for U.S. veterans in recognition of Veterans Day. The NHL’s partnership with ForgiveCo will provide debt relief and aid to more than 600 veterans and their families. This season, all 32 Clubs are saluting and honoring military members, veterans, and their families with themed games or special in-game moments. Tonight’s 2026 NHL Veterans Appreciation Night on TNT Sports Platforms presented by Navy Federal Credit Union doubleheader will feature the Sabres and the Golden Knights at home, with both Clubs hosting their annual military appreciation night. The broadcast will include interviews with Sabres forward Tage Thompson who sponsors ‘Tickets for Troops,’ and Golden Knights defenseman Noah Hanifin, who has multiple family members who have served. Tonight, the Sabres and Golden Knights are also hosting veterans who are recipients of the debt relief initiative. Of the $1.5 million of debt being erased, $400,000 is directly supporting veterans in Western New York and $500,000 is directly supporting veterans in Las Vegas, Nevada. In Buffalo, U.S. Army veteran Milton J. Nolan is attending the game with his family. Nolan served four years on active duty, including during Desert Storm, as well as service in Korea. Through Operation Line Shift, medical debt due to his battle with appendix cancer was erased. In Las Vegas, U.S. Army veteran James King is attending the game with his family. King served for eight years, and his medical debt associated with his wife’s hospitalization was erased. items.body: TORONTO -- All is quiet between the Minnesota Wild and Quinn Hughes , and the team could keep the defenseman past the NHL Trade Deadline on March 1 if he doesn’t sign a new deal, general manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday. Hughes, whom the Wild acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a trade Dec. 12, 2025, is in the final season of a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) he signed with Vancouver on Oct. 3, 2021. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1. If he doesn’t sign before June 30, he will become an unrestricted free agent the next day. On Oct. 24, Hughes said he “wouldn’t be surprised if something happens soon.” But Tuesday, Guerin said the situation is “status quo.” “Because, honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” Would Guerin be willing to keep Hughes past the trade deadline? Hughes won the Norris Trophy as the NHL’s best defenseman in 2024. Since the trade, Hughes has 80 points (11 goals, 69 assists) in 68 games, second on the Wild and second among NHL defensemen. In that span, forward Kirill Kaprizov leads Minnesota with 87 points (44 goals, 43 assists) in 67 games, and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers is first among NHL defensemen with 98 points (26 goals, 72 assists) in 70 games. The Wild (13-3-4), who extended their point streak to nine games (7-0-2) with a 2-1 overtime win at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday, lead the Central Division. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.”

items.summary: The scene as Montreal paid tribute to Carey Price before Tuesday’s game will stay with the Canadiens and goaltender Jacob Fowler forever.
items.body: MONTREAL — Shortly before taking the ice to one of the most rousing ovations in Bell Centre history, Carey Price was asked for his favourite memory in the building he called home for 15 years. “Probably that night with Patrick (Roy’s jersey) retirement,” Price said. “That was really special, and I have a picture of that in my memorabilia room. It’s pretty special to be part of something like this.” That was one special evening. Nov. 22, 2008, the night 33 was immortalized. No one remembers that it ended with Price fittingly making 33 saves and not so fittingly losing 3-2 in the shootout to the Boston Bruins. Least of all him, apparently. For Price could’ve chosen any of the 202 wins he registered in a Montreal Canadiens home uniform as his most cherished memory. He could’ve referenced one of the 22 wins he recorded when it mattered most in front of these fans—in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. But the night Price watched his hero have his number retired was the one that stayed with the goaltender more than any other because it reinforced how special it is to be a Canadien and reconnected him with his childhood dream. It is the shared dream of every hockey-loving child, but certainly the ones with true NHL aspirations. They don’t close their eyes and picture playing in the three-quarter full buildings of tax-free states. They don’t think about the comfort anonymity provides in a sunbelt market. No, the dream is playing out a Hall of Fame career in a mecca like Montreal, of leaving it all on the ice for fans who chant your name at full throat until they go hoarse. The fantasy is coming back for one more dose of that, like Roy did almost exactly 18 years to the day Price did. items.body: Searching for consistency away from home, Colorado opens with win at Toronto TORONTO -- The Colorado Avalanche will know by the end of this stretch of four straight road games if they are rounding into the team they believe they can and should be this season. "Yeah, I mean, you have to be a dominant team at home and then you have to be a very good road team," Avalanche forward Gabriel Landeskog said. "If you want to be that dominant team that you want to be and go where you want to go that is most definitely the objective." The Avalanche got off to a strong start to their four-game road stretch with a 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday. But what happens next in Ottawa on Thursday, then in Montreal on Saturday and finally in Utah a week from Wednesday will either allow them to feel settled into the season or continue what has been a topsy-turvy first quarter for the Stanley Cup contender. You never want to place too much emphasis on a stretch of four games in an 84-game season, and the Avalanche (11-6-2) aren't doing that, but they feel the importance of these four games, especially considering what road life has been like for them so far this season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Ottawa Senators suffered a tough 3-2 overtime loss to the Washington Capitals on Tuesday, but the well-being of forward Nick Cousins is their biggest concern coming out of the game. Late in the third period, Cousins was picking up the puck deep in his own zone and got absolutely hammered by a crushing body check from Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun. The hit sent Cousins careening into the glass, and he lay motionless on the ice for some time before eventually getting helped to the Senators’ dressing room. Since the hit targeted Cousins’ chest and Chychrun did not leave his feet, there was no penalty assessed on the play. After the game, Senators head coach Travis Green gave a less than promising update on Cousins’ status. Cousins, 33, has two goals and an assist for three points in 19 games this played this season. Last season, he put up nine goals and 14 assists for 23 points in 81 games before contributing no goals and an assist in Ottawa’s first-round playoff loss to the Carolina Hurricanes in four games. Selected by the Philadelphia Flyers in the third round of the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, the Belleville, Ontario native has played for six different teams over 13 NHL seasons. Best known as an agitator and bottom-six forechecker, Cousins has never put up more than 27 points in a season, a number he reached in the 2018-19 season with the Arizona Coyotes, and then again in the 2022-23 season with the Florida Panthers . He won a Stanley Cup with the Panthers in the 2023-24 season. Given the impact of Chychrun’s hit, the concern is that Cousins suffered a concussion. items.body: Fresh off Hockey Hall of Fame initiation, former Canadiens goalie honored in front of home crowd MIN@MTL: Price gets ovations on joining Canadiens' Ring of Honor It took four minutes for the fans at the Bell Centre to get back in their seats after Carey Price took the ice. The former Montreal Canadiens goaltender – and now a member of the 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class – was honored on Tuesday at the arena he called home for his entire 15-year NHL career. As he was introduced, fans gave him a standing ovation which lasted four whole minutes before he addressed the crowd. Chants of “Carey! Carey!” and “Ole! Ole!” rang out as Price took it all in. L'ovation debout de quatre minutes la plus méritée de l'histoire The most well-deserved four-minute standing ovation #GoHabsGo | @CP0031 pic.twitter.com/ehAzCiXF0Z Tuesday’s addition to the Canadiens’ Ring of Honour comes a day after Price’s induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday in Toronto. Price – the Canadiens’ all-time winningest goalie – was drafted by Montreal in the first round of the 2005 NHL Draft, making his debut with the team in the 2007 season. He played his entire career with the Canadiens until his retirement in 2022. He finished his career with a 361-261-79 record and a .917 save percentage with 49 shutouts. In his career-defining 2014-15 season, Price swept the individual NHL awards, winning the William M. Jennings Trophy, Vezina Trophy, Ted Lindsay Award and the Hart Memorial Trophy. He added the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy in the 2021-22 season.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Heinen, Hanifin, Marchment, Panthers By Bradley Keith | at November 10, 2026 7:54 pm According to Aaron Portzline of The Athletic , Columbus forward Danton Heinen did not “immediately” report to AHL Cleveland last week after he cleared waivers . The veteran is reportedly weighing his options while the Blue Jackets organization is giving him the time needed to figure out next steps in his career. Coming up on a decade since his 47-point debut campaign in Boston, the 31-year-old has become more of a rotational depth forward at this point in his career and no longer the strong third line two-way winger he once was. Still, it’s not hard to see why Heinen would want to assess where his career goes next. The 2014 fourth-round pick (Boston) has skated in just 17 AHL games since the 2016-17 season as a prospect. A 12-game stint with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins last season proved he still had more in the tank, dominating with 17 points in 12 games. Heinen accepted a two-way deal to stick around in Ohio for the season, making the team but coming away scoreless in his 10 games, averaging 10:10 a night, the lowest usage of his 11-year career. Currently 26th in the AHL the Monsters already have a roster full of veterans including Steven Lorentz , who has lit it up with seven goals in nine games, as well as Carson Soucy who just joined the club. Whatever happens ahead, Columbus respectfully is making sure they do right of the British Columbia native who has skated in 622 NHL games in his career.

Ducks head coach Joel Quenneville said Tuesday that Terry is “likely” to play as the Ducks welcome the Predators to the Honda Center on Wednesday. The Denver product added three goals and 11 points in 12 playoff contests as the Ducks defeated the Edmonton Oilers in the first round before being eliminated by the Vegas Golden Knights . A four-time 20-goal scorer, Terry has consistently been one of the Ducks’ most dangerous offensive players since establishing himself as an NHL regular in the 2020-21 season. In his absence, the Ducks have gotten off to a 10-7-1 start to the 2026-27 season, posting a plus-3 goal differential. The Ducks originally selected Terry in the fifth round (No. 148 overall) of the 2015 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ right wing spent his first three post-draft seasons playing close to home at the University of Denver, suiting up for Team USA along the way at both the 2017 World Juniors and the 2018 Winter Olympics. items.summary: The Montreal Canadiens welcomed Carey Price back to the Bell Centre with a memorable, spine-tingling ovation Tuesday night.
items.body: MONTREAL — The Montreal Canadiens welcomed Carey Price back to the Bell Centre with a memorable, spine-tingling ovation Tuesday night. Canadiens fans cheered for close to four minutes during an on-ice ceremony, wildly serenading their longtime star goaltender with a blend of “Ca-rey! Ca-rey!” and “Olé, Olé” chants ahead of puck drop against the Minnesota Wild. Price, meanwhile, stood beside the team benches, next to the five individual trophies he won over his illustrious career, as he attempted to get a word in. “From the bottom of my heart, the most sincere ‘Merci beaucoup,’” Price told the crowd, his voice trembling. Following team tradition, the Canadiens added Price to their ring of honour after his induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday in Toronto. Price, 39, became the 62nd member of the Canadiens organization to enter the Hall of Fame, capping a remarkable journey that began in the remote community of Anahim Lake, B.C. Growing up, Price’s father, Jerry, flew his son in a four-seat plane 320 kilometres from their hometown to Williams Lake, B.C., three times a week so he could play minor hockey. Price went on to spend his entire 15-year NHL career in Montreal after the Canadiens selected him fifth overall in the 2005 draft, becoming the franchise’s all-time leader with 361 wins. He finished with a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts in 712 regular-season games. items.title: Maple Leafs’ Chayka understands Tanev’s reaction to load management
items.body: TORONTO — Count Toronto Maple Leafs GM John Chayka among those not surprised to hear defenceman Chris Tanev 's reaction to the team’s load management plan that will ration his use over the course of the season. Chayka expected as much when asked about Tanev's response at the NHL's general manager meetings on Tuesday in downtown Toronto. “I think it’s natural and actually a good sign that he wants to play every game,” Chayka said. “It’s Chris Tanev. He’s made a career out of being that player and takes a lot of pride in being available to play every night. “From our side, we do have an obligation to the players and to the organization to do the right thing and consider a player’s long-term health. And to do the right thing for the organization for the short-term and long-term. We respect that Chris wants to play.” Tanev, 36, missed all but 11 games last season after sustaining a serious concussion. This season, he suffered an injury on Oct. 10 against the Colorado Avalanche and then missed nine games. Coach Jim Hiller said that while he wished he could have Tanev in the lineup each night, “there’s a plan in place to protect the player and the team.” Chayka said: “We’re taking in a lot of information and making decisions. It’s my decision and I think it’s the right one for the organization.” It’s also not final. If Tanev’s health improves, the Maple Leafs are open to amending their plan. “This is an ongoing discussion,” Chayka said. “As Chris builds up some resiliency and the doctors get comfortable with where he’s at, then we’ll change our minds as it makes sense to do so.” In the here and now, Tanev's situation is just one of a handful that Chayka is monitoring as injuries mount for the Maple Leafs. items.title: Hellebuyck sends mixed message to Jets fans seeking closure
items.summary: In Connor Hellebuyck’s careful attempt to prevent this from becoming a sticky situation, he has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known.
items.body: WINNIPEG — In his much-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday, Connor Hellebuyck desperately tried to keep his story straight. But in his careful attempt to prevent his departure from Winnipeg from becoming a sticky situation, the former franchise goaltender has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known. Sitting in front of dozens of reporters at Canada Life Centre, Hellebuyck looked and acted like a man wanting to have his cake and eat it, too. Rather than speak clearly and concisely about the treatment he received from disappointed Canadians and a clear desire to move his family south of the border, Hellebuyck opted to dance around the subject. Only adding insult to injury, Hellebuyck won't even face the music Tuesday against his former team. Despite his insistence that he felt a "duty" to play, New Jersey Devils general manager Sunny Mehta stepped in with a dizzying analytics-led excuse. Citing a "reduction in our expected win probability," Mehta is sitting his all-star goalie. The irony of Hellebuyck demanding out of Winnipeg, where he had full control of his playing time, to join an organization that now dictates his ice time through analytics is too difficult to ignore. But to understand just how brazen it was for Hellebuyck to sit at a table inside Canada Life Centre and ask fans to separate his exit from his legacy, you have to look at how that exit played out. "The day I said I was a Jet for life, I meant it," Hellebuyck said. "But I also didn't foresee the future that was going to happen." That future turned out to be a sudden and steep decline for a team that had claimed the Presidents' Trophy as the NHL's best regular-season team just a year earlier. items.title: NHL to explore replay assist technology for officials
items.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman was quick to remind that wholesale changes won’t be coming to the way the game is officiated, but he mentioned how tech advancements might streamline everything from information to the flow of the game.
items.body: TORONTO — Remember a few weeks ago when Buffalo’s Owen Power was incensed that he was wrongly whistled for a high-sticking penalty? It was friendly fire. Power didn’t high-stick Matvei Michkov, who was done dirty by his own teammate, Trevor Zegras. All 18,000 fans in KeyBank Arena in Buffalo saw it on replay. The NHL’s Situation Room saw it in near real time. But once the call is made on the ice, according to current rules, there’s no chance to review it and it cannot be rescinded. “The only four people that don’t get to see it are the four guys in striped shirts,” NHL senior executive vice president of hockey operations Colin Campbell said. “There’s times we would like to get involved.” To that end, Campbell said the NHL will explore in the coming months how things like rapid replay assist technology can aid on-ice officials. Think something that wouldn’t involve a long huddle or review, but how quickly, as in the NFL, the spot of the ball is corrected, or how fast it is relayed to the officiating team that a runner stepped out of bounds. “The game’s not perfect,” Campbell said. “How can we help them out? “You look at football, what they’ve done with the quarterback’s helmet. You look at baseball, with the pitcher and catcher (pitchcom device). All sports are expanding communication.” The discussion was brought to the NHL’s 32 general managers in their meeting on Tuesday and Campbell said the “appetite was good.” Rule changes cannot be enacted mid-season but can be voted on in Florida in March for the Competition Committee to implement for 2027-28. items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap will be $113.5 million next season, and is projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The NHL’s salary cap has increased substantially over the last couple of seasons, leading to some monstrous contracts getting handed out this past offseason. It’s expected to continue to skyrocket in the years to come. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , however, the league is looking at the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap’s growth over the next two seasons. At Tuesday’s GM meetings, it was decided that the NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss ways of making the salary cap’s increases over the next couple seasons less dramatic year over year, with the hopes of creating a more stable salary environment across the league. The NHL’s salary cap this season is $104 million, which increased from $95.5 million last season and $88 million the season prior. It will grow to $113.5 million next season, and is currently projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season. According to Friedman, one strategy the league could pursue is raising next season’s cap from $113.5 million by a certain amount, and then lowering the 2028-29 cap by the same amount, thereby shrinking the cap spike between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. For example, if next year’s cap is raised from $113.5 to $115.5 million, representing a $2 million bump, then the cap for the 2028-29 season would be decreased by $2 million, going from a projected $127.5 million to a projected $125.5 million. This would keep the difference between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 salary caps to $10 million. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources It was a crucial day of action in Denmark on Tuesday. While some teams looked to fine-tune themselves ahead of the quarterfinals, other teams were battling to move up into the top four of their respective groups and avoid relegation. Let’s break down how each game played out, and who shone brightly for their team: Remember how people were picking on the revamped tournament format? Well, in the olden days, this wouldn’t have happened. Czechia entered the tournament as the presumed favorites to finish second in Group A, but that is being tested after a gutsy effort by a German team on the rise. The Germans really pushed the Czechs around for long stretches of the game, with Lilli Welcke breaking the ice just over a minute into the contest. Czechia kept on the attack, however, with Linda Vocetkova potting her second goal in as many games near the halfway mark of the frame. We saw a goaltending duel from then on. Germany’s Sandra Abstreiter and Czechia’s Klara Peslarova both came up with big saves for the remainder of regulation, forcing overtime. Despite numerous chances in the extra frame, a shootout was required. items.title: Wild activate Jared Spurgeon off injured reserve
items.summary: Minnesota has also assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to the AHL’s Iowa Wild.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are welcoming their captain back into the fold. On Tuesday, the Wild announced that they have activated defenseman Jared Spurgeon off of injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Wild have assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Iowa Wild. Spurgeon, 36, has missed Minnesota’s last five games , and was also out for a four-game stretch with an upper-body injury earlier this season. In 10 games played so far, the Edmonton native has a goal and four assists for five points while averaging about 20 and a half minutes of ice time. Last season, Spurgeon notched six goals and 16 assists for 22 points in 79 games while averaging about 19 and a half minutes of ice time. He then put up no goals and an assist while averaging a tick over 21 minutes in 11 playoff games. Selected by the New York Islanders in the sixth round of the 2008 NHL Entry Draft, Spurgeon did not sign his entry-level deal with New York and instead signed with Minnesota after his five-year junior career with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Spurgeon is now in his 17th NHL season, all with the Wild. He ranks second in games played on Minnesota’s all-time list with 1,022, just six games back of Mikko Koivu. He also ranks third on the Wild’s all-time scoring list with 443 points. He is in the final season of a seven-year, $53.03 million contract . Pitlick, 35, has gone scoreless in 12 games played for Minnesota this season. The Minneapolis, Minnesota native has played for nine different teams over parts of 12 seasons in the NHL. Minnesota kicks off a three-game road trip against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday before visiting the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday.
